title: Sheaves of Lambda-modules on the small etale site form a Grothendieck abelian category
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $T_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $\Lambda_T$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $\Lambda$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)=\Mod(\Lambda_T)$ the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it is abelian, it has all small colimits, filtered colimits in it are exact, and it has a generator, namely $\bigoplus_{U\in\mathcal S}j_{U!}\Lambda_U$, where $\mathcal S$ is a set of affine objects of $T_{\Et}$ such that every object of $T_{\Et}$ has a covering by members of $\mathcal S$, and $j_{U!}\Lambda_U$ is the extension by zero of $\Lambda_T|_U$ (Stacks 03DI), i.e. the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf of $\Lambda_T$-modules $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}_{T_{\Et}}(V,U)}\Lambda_T(V)$. In particular (case $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$) the category $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] is Grothendieck abelian.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DA (label lemma-abelian: Mod(O) is abelian), Lemma 03DB (label lemma-limits-colimits: all limits and colimits exist, filtered colimits are exact), Lemma 03EW (label lemma-module-quotient-flat, part (3): every O-module is a quotient of a direct sum of modules j_{U!}O_U, which gives the generator); the small etale site as a site with a set of objects: Topologies, Definitions 021A and 021B (literature/stacks-project/topologies.tex); the statement is used in Cohomology on Sites, proof of Lemma 07AC (label lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex, line 9345: 'the category of modules on a ringed site is a Grothendieck abelian category')

proof.text: Use the constant-ring module equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constant-ring-module-equivalence]. The category of ModuleCat(ULift Λ)-valued sheaves is Grothendieck abelian by the existing small-etale sheaf instances; IsGrothendieckAbelian.of_equivalence transfers this structure to module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf. This proves the first conjunct without the colimit/forgetful construction.

Index the family by T.AffineEtale itself (which lies in Type (u+1)) and take U to be AffineEtale.Spec. All sources are spectra, hence affine. For V index covering arrows by the sigma type of pairs (i,f:U(i)→V). Cover density says the sieve of arrows factoring through Spec is covering. Each such factorization is in Sieve.ofArrows of this sigma-indexed family, so the latter sieve is covering. This realizes [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover] at the universe of the statement without selecting a skeleton.

For each i, let Q(i) be the sheafification of the free module on uliftYoneda(U(i)). Compose sheafificationAdjunction.homEquiv, freeHomEquiv and uliftYonedaEquiv to identify maps Q(i)→M with sections of M over U(i). Naturality on composition follows successively from the two adjunction naturality identities and uliftYonedaEquiv_comp. The lift of a section therefore tests the component of any sheaf morphism on that section. ULift changes only the universe of represented morphisms.

If two maps agree after every map out of the Q(i), the naturality calculation of the preceding step shows their underlying abelian presheaf components agree on every affine object and every section. Functor.whiskerLeft_obj_map_bijective_of_isCoverDense reflects this equality from the affine dense subsite to the full site. Faithfulness of the underlying-presheaf functor then gives equality of the module sheaf maps. Thus Q is a separating family.

Grothendieck abelianness from the first step supplies the coproduct of Q. Take its standard colimit cofan, whose colimit witness is colimit.isColimit, and apply ObjectProperty.IsSeparating.isSeparator_coproduct. Combine this generator with the affine-cover witnesses and the first conjunct. The abelian sheaf conjunct is the existing small-etale Grothendieck-abelian instance [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck].

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks sites-modules 03DA (abelian), 03DB (colimits, exact filtered colimits), 03DI/03EW (generator j_{U!}O_U with Hom = F(U)), with the set of affine étale objects from Topologies 021B/04HR. Six steps. Created four nodes: lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful (unsplit: Mod(O) colimits as sheafified sectionwise colimits, forgetful functor to Ab faithful, exact, commuting with colimits; Mathlib has the pieces but not that toSheaf preserves colimits), lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module (Mathlib leaf PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaEquiv), lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover (Mathlib leaf: AffineEtale.instEssentiallySmall + IsCoverDense), lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck (Mathlib leaf: isGrothendieckAbelian_sheaf_smallEtaleTopology with A = AddCommGrpCat). The statement's generator was made explicit: j_{U!}Λ_U for étale (not open) U → T is defined as the sheafification of V ↦ ⊕_{Mor(V,U)} Λ_T(V) (Stacks 03DI), which needs def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification (added to stmt_deps); the open-immersion nodes def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero / lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction do not apply to étale U → T and are not used; lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-free-separator is for A-valued sheaves Sh(C,J;A), not Mod(O), and is not used (the separator argument is written out for Mod(O)). Searches: loogle shows a newer Mathlib has SheafOfModules.instIsGrothendieckAbelian (small C only), absent from the pinned Mathlib.
